## Google Drive Folder Auto-Backup to Dropbox

Every file that lands in your important Google Drive folder gets a second copy in Dropbox within minutes - cross-provider backup for the documents you can't lose.

**Setup time:** 10 minutes  ·  **Level:** Beginner

**You'll need accounts/credentials for:** Google Drive, Dropbox

**Replace these before running:**
- `REPLACE_WITH_YOUR_FOLDER`

**Setup steps:**
1. Connect Google Drive and pick the folder to watch in the trigger node.
2. Connect Dropbox (create an app at dropbox.com/developers with files.content.write scope) and set the destination path.
3. Activate, then drop a test file into the Drive folder and check Dropbox a minute later.

Free templates and updates: navkhan103.github.io

### How it runs

Starts from **New File in Folder**.

1. A Google Drive Trigger fires when a file is created in your chosen folder.
2. A Google Drive node downloads the file's binary content.
3. A Dropbox node uploads it to your backup folder, keeping the original filename.

### If something breaks

The read and AI nodes here **retry 3× automatically** (5s apart), which absorbs rate limits and brief timeouts.

Nodes that **send or write deliberately do not retry** — a send that reached the far end but lost its response would otherwise fire twice, so you'd get duplicate messages or duplicate rows.

To be told when one of those fails, build a workflow starting with an **Error Trigger** node that posts to Slack or email, then set it under **three-dot menu > Settings > Error Workflow**. Do it once and point every workflow at it.
